codon.ui.help.start.title: Start debugging
codon.ui.help.start.body: Aim at a command block and press %s to toggle its breakpoint. Trigger the command normally. When execution pauses, press %s to switch between the cursor and the world. Select a context, inspect its state, then step or continue.
codon.ui.help.breakpoints.title: Block and function breakpoints
codon.ui.help.breakpoints.body: Use /codon breakpoint block <x> <y> <z> or /codon breakpoint function <function> <line> to toggle a breakpoint. Use /codon breakpoint list to list them, or /codon breakpoint clear to remove all of them. These commands require command permissions.
codon.ui.help.stop.title: Marker colors
codon.ui.help.stop.body: Orange (amber) marks the current stopped command block, with a point in its center. Other block breakpoints have red outlines. Teal marks execution anchors and facing. In execute flow, green means a context was created and red means a context was excluded; these do not mean blocks or entities were created or deleted.
codon.ui.help.camera.title: Move around while paused
codon.ui.help.hide_ui.title: See the game HUD
codon.ui.help.hide_ui.body: In the debugger or world, hold %s to hide debugger panels and markers while keeping chat, the scoreboard, and the action bar visible. Release it to restore the debugger. This does not change the execution state. Change this binding in Options > Controls > Key Binds.
codon.ui.help.camera.body: Close this guide first. %s switches cursor / freecam. Use %s / %s / %s / %s to move, %s / %s to move up / down, and %s to move faster. Cursor mode lets you click debugger controls. Key labels here follow your current bindings.
codon.ui.help.control.resume: Resume execution until another breakpoint is reached or the command finishes.
codon.ui.help.control.over: Advance to the next command stage at the same or a shallower call depth. Nested function execution is stepped over.
codon.ui.help.control.into: Pause at the next command stage, including stages inside a called function. A step is a command stage, not a game tick.
codon.ui.help.control.out: Run until execution returns to a shallower call depth. At the outermost level, stop when execution completes.
codon.ui.help.availability.title: When controls are available
codon.ui.help.availability.body: Step and continue controls are enabled while paused. They are disabled while waiting for the server to acknowledge a request. Use these shortcuts in the debugger or world after closing this guide.
codon.ui.help.gizmo.title: Grouped gizmos
codon.ui.help.gizmo.body: The gizmo button cycles grouped and individual labels. In grouped mode, click an overlapping-context group to open its contexts in the inspector, then choose the context you want to examine.
codon.ui.help.labels.title: Individual labels
codon.ui.help.labels.body: Show separate context labels where space permits. Click a label to select its execution context. A context number links a world label to the corresponding inspector entry.
codon.ui.help.details.title: Inspector
codon.ui.help.details.body: Show or hide Contexts and the selected context's details with this toolbar button. Scroll over the context list to see additional entries. Call stack and execute flow are in the command panel below the world.
codon.ui.help.source.title: What is a context?
codon.ui.help.source.body: A context holds the executor, position, dimension and facing used by a command. It is not always an entity. Select one to inspect its anchor coordinates and rotation. Selecting a context changes what you inspect; it does not move the entity.
codon.ui.help.flow.title: Read execute flow
codon.ui.help.flow.body: An execution context holds the executor, position, dimension, and rotation used by a command. Click a recorded clause to inspect its contexts and world markers. Counts show input → output contexts; runs and successes are separate. An ellipsis (...) means the value has not been measured; 0 is a measured zero. A warning icon marks incomplete recording. Hover the icon for details about missing input/output links or omitted data. Recorded counts may not describe the full execution. Amber marks the actual stopped clause, teal marks the clause being inspected. Unobserved text has no recorded counts. Arrows follow recorded execution order, including function calls and returns. Expand the panel or scroll to read longer commands.
codon.ui.help.created.title: Created context (+)
codon.ui.help.created.body: Green marks a context created at the selected flow stage, for example when execute branches into multiple contexts. It does not mean an entity was summoned.
codon.ui.help.excluded.title: Excluded context (-)
codon.ui.help.excluded.body: Red marks a context filtered out at this stage. It does not continue along that branch. This is separate from the red outline used for other block breakpoints.
codon.ui.help.offscreen.title: Outside the viewport
codon.ui.help.offscreen.body: The selected context is outside the visible world area or in another dimension. Read its dimension and anchor in the inspector. A missing world label does not by itself mean the context was removed.
codon.ui.help.uuid.title: Copy executor UUID
codon.ui.help.uuid.body: Click the copy icon in context details to copy the selected entity executor UUID. Position-only contexts do not have an entity UUID.
codon.ui.help.stack.title: Call stack and command
codon.ui.help.stack.body: Call stack shows the frames recorded with the command you are inspecting, including functions that have already returned. Click a frame to inspect its caller while keeping the same stack available. Scroll horizontally over the call path to browse all frames; the mouse wheel works too. Caller and historical contexts are read-only; selecting them does not rewind execution. Current restores the actual stopped command and its live call stack.
codon.ui.help.watch.title: Add a watch
codon.ui.help.watch.body: Click + beside Watches to add a watch. Choose its type and enter or browse an objective or NBT path. Leave Entity blank to follow the selected context, or choose an entity to bind it. Enter adds the watch; Ctrl+Enter keeps the form open for another. Edit, pin and remove watches directly in the Watches window.
codon.ui.help.types.title: Watch types and inputs
codon.ui.help.types.body: Score: enter a scoreboard objective for the selected executor. Entity NBT: enter an NBT path such as Health. Storage NBT: enter a storage ID such as example:state and an NBT path. Entity-dependent watches need an entity executor.
codon.ui.help.pin.title: Follow selection or pin an entity
codon.ui.help.pin.body: Score and Entity NBT watches follow the selected context when Entity is blank. Choose an entity in the form or use the pin beside a saved Watch to fix its target. Unpin to follow context again. Storage uses its storage ID instead.
codon.ui.help.values.title: Read watch values
codon.ui.help.values.body: Watches shows saved expressions first, followed by changes at this pause. The field and current value are on the first line; the second names its target and whether it follows context. Amber arrows show value changes. Click a row to inspect and copy full values. Previous executor identifies a completed change from the context just stepped. Use Retry for unavailable reads.
codon.ui.help.nbt.title: Explore entity NBT
codon.ui.help.nbt.body: Select an entity context to browse its NBT in the context inspector. NBT is always shown for the selected live entity. Expand compound or list fields to inspect children. Scroll to load additional fields automatically, and use Refresh NBT when offered. Hover a field for its path and preview. Pinned fields remain in Watches when you switch contexts.
codon.ui.help.nbt_pin.title: Pin directly from NBT
codon.ui.help.nbt_pin.body: Left-click a field pin to add or remove a watch for that entity. Right-click to add the same path for all available entity contexts, or remove those watches when all are already pinned. Unsupported paths cannot be pinned.
